memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
The LORD said to Moses, "Tell Aaron and his sons to treat with respect
the sacred offerings the Israelites consecrate to me, so they will not
profane my holy name. I am the LORD" - Lev 22:1-2 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The offerings the Israelites brought were not ordinary food. A family
had set them apart for God, sometimes at real cost. So the priests who
handled them were told plainly: treat these with respect.

There is a danger that comes with familiarity. The priests handled
sacred things every single day. Day after day, year after year, the
extraordinary can start to feel routine. God knew that, and He warned
them before it happened.

Dear friend, the same danger sits quietly in our lives. We can sing
the same worship songs without hearing the words. We can read a
chapter of Scripture while our mind is already on the day's tasks. We
can take the bread and cup at communion the way we take a snack. The
things themselves are still holy. Our hearts have simply gone numb.

Paul warned the Corinthians about exactly this, urging them to examine
themselves before eating the bread and drinking the cup (1 Cor
11:28-29). Not to make them fearful, but to make them awake.

The cure is not more rules. It is remembering who we are dealing with.
"I am the LORD." Sit with that today before you rush into anything
else.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Where has familiarity dulled my sense of God's holiness?
2. When did I last approach worship with genuine attention?
3. What one spiritual habit have I been doing on autopilot?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Father, forgive me for handling holy things with a casual heart. Wake
me up again to who You are, and let me never grow bored of Your
presence. Amen.
